```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 6, dpi = 110)
old <- options(rmarkdown.html_vignette.check_title = FALSE)
```

**`cfbfastR` is an R package that gives you college football play-by-play data
with expected points added (EPA) and win probability already computed on every
play, plus clients for the CollegeFootballData.com (CFBD) and ESPN APIs.** You
can go from a fresh R install to a chart comparing every FBS offense and defense
in about twenty lines of code, without an API key. This page walks through
exactly that, then explains the columns, the vocabulary, and where to go next.

If you have never written R before, that is fine. Read top to bottom and run
each code block in order.

## What you'll learn

- How to install R, RStudio and `cfbfastR`
- Where `cfbfastR` gets its data, and how a function's name tells you its source
- How to get and register a free CollegeFootballData.com API key
- How to load a full season of play-by-play with [`load_cfb_pbp()`](../reference/load_cfb_pbp.html)
- How to compute **EPA per play** and **success rate** for every offense and defense
- How to make your first `ggplot2` chart of team efficiency
- What the core play-by-play columns mean, and the vocabulary analysts use
  (EP, EPA, WP, WPA, success rate, havoc, garbage time, and more)

## Step 1: Install R and RStudio

R is the language; RStudio is the editor most people use to write it. Both are
free.

1. Download R from <https://cran.r-project.org>, choosing your operating system
   (Windows, macOS or Linux), and install the latest release.
2. Download RStudio Desktop from
   [posit.co](https://posit.co/download/rstudio-desktop/) and install it.
3. **Windows only:** install [Rtools](https://cran.r-project.org/bin/windows/Rtools/)
   that matches your R version. It is not an R package; it is the toolchain R
   uses to build packages from source, which you need for development versions
   from GitHub.
4. Keep the [RStudio IDE cheatsheet](https://rstudio.github.io/cheatsheets/html/rstudio-ide.html)
   open while you learn the layout.

## Step 2: Install cfbfastR

| Source | Command | When to use it |
|---|---|---|
| CRAN | `install.packages("cfbfastR")` | the stable release; start here |
| GitHub (with `pak`) | `pak::pak("sportsdataverse/cfbfastR")` | the development version, with the newest functions and fixes |
| GitHub (with `remotes`) | `remotes::install_github("sportsdataverse/cfbfastR")` | same as above, if you already use `remotes` |

```{r install, eval=FALSE}
install.packages("cfbfastR")

# or the development version:
if (!requireNamespace("pak", quietly = TRUE)) install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("sportsdataverse/cfbfastR")

# the examples on this page also use dplyr and ggplot2
install.packages(c("dplyr", "ggplot2"))
```

Then load the packages at the top of every script:

```{r libraries}
# Do not add an install step for cfbfastR here. pkgdown and R CMD check
# render this article against the package being built; installing the
# CRAN release would overwrite that dev build, and any function added
# since the last release would vanish mid-render.
library(cfbfastR)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

## Step 3: Know where the data comes from

`cfbfastR` reads from a few distinct sources, and **the prefix of every function
name tells you which one** — and therefore whether you need an API key.

| Prefix | Source | API key? | What you get |
|---|---|---|---|
| `load_cfb_*()` | pre-built season files on the SportsDataverse GitHub releases | no | play-by-play with EPA/WPA, schedules, rosters, teams, ratings, recruiting |
| `load_espn_cfb_*()` | pre-built ESPN season files on GitHub releases | no | ESPN play-by-play, box scores, drives and advanced stats |
| `load_ncaa_mfb_*()` | pre-built stats.ncaa.org season files on GitHub releases | no | play-by-play, box scores and rosters including FCS and lower divisions |
| `cfbd_*()` | the [CollegeFootballData.com API](https://collegefootballdata.com) | **yes (free)** | games, drives, plays, stats, ratings (SP+, SRS, Elo, FPI), recruiting, betting lines, draft |
| `espn_cfb_*()`, `espn_*()` | ESPN's public APIs, live | no | scoreboards, game summaries, live play-by-play, rankings, FPI |
| `fox_cfb_*()`, `yahoo_cfb_*()` | Fox Sports and Yahoo Sports APIs, live | no | box scores, standings, odds, season stats |
| `calculate_*()` | the models shipped with `cfbfastR` | no | score your own plays with the EP, WP, fourth-down and related models |
| `update_cfb_db()` | GitHub releases, written to a local database | no | a SQLite (or other DBI) copy of every season of play-by-play |

As a rule of thumb: **reach for a `load_*()` function first.** It downloads a
whole season in one request, is fast, and needs no key. Use `cfbd_*()` when you
need something the release files do not carry, and the live `espn_cfb_*()`
functions for games in progress.

How many functions sit in each family, counted from the installed package:

```{r function-families}
exports <- getNamespaceExports("cfbfastR")
families <- c("load_cfb_", "load_espn_cfb_", "load_ncaa_mfb_", "cfbd_",
              "espn_", "fox_cfb_", "yahoo_cfb_", "calculate_")
data.frame(
  prefix = paste0(families, "*()"),
  functions = vapply(families, function(p) sum(startsWith(exports, p)), integer(1)),
  row.names = NULL
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Step 4: Get a free CollegeFootballData.com API key

You do **not** need a key for the worked example below — it uses
`load_cfb_pbp()`. You do need one for any `cfbd_*()` function.

1. Go to <https://collegefootballdata.com/key> and enter your e-mail address.
   The free tier is enough for everything on this site.
2. The key arrives by e-mail. Copy it.
3. Tell R about it. For the current session only:

```{r key-session, eval=FALSE}
Sys.setenv(CFBD_API_KEY = "YOUR-API-KEY-HERE")
```

To save it for every session, add it to your `.Renviron` file. The easiest way
to open that file is `usethis::edit_r_environ()`. Add this line (no quotes),
save, then restart R (**Session → Restart R**, or `Ctrl + Shift + F10`):

```
CFBD_API_KEY=YOUR-API-KEY-HERE
```

4. Check that it worked:

```{r key-check, eval=FALSE}
cfbfastR::has_cfbd_key()       # TRUE if CFBD_API_KEY is set
cfbfastR::cfbd_api_key_info()  # your Patreon tier and remaining calls
```

Never paste your key into a script you share or commit to GitHub — keep it in
`.Renviron`. The [API key help page](../reference/register_cfbd.html) has the
full details.

With a key registered, every `cfbd_*()` function works. For example:

```{r cfbd-example, eval=FALSE}
# needs a CFBD API key -- not run when this page is built
cfbd_game_info(year = 2025, team = "Texas")
cfbd_ratings_sp(year = 2025)
```

## Step 5: Load a season of play-by-play

Now the fun part. One call downloads every play of a season, already scored by
the expected points and win probability models. We use **2025**, the most
recent complete season; change the number to load any season from 2014 on, or
pass a range such as `2021:2025`.

```{r load-pbp}
season <- 2025
pbp <- load_cfb_pbp(season)
```

```{r pbp-size, include=FALSE}
n_rows  <- nrow(pbp)
n_cols  <- ncol(pbp)
n_games <- dplyr::n_distinct(pbp$game_id)
```

That is `r format(n_rows, big.mark = ",")` rows (one per play) and
`r n_cols` columns across `r format(n_games, big.mark = ",")` games. The most
useful columns sit on the left. Here are a few plays:

```{r peek}
pbp |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(EPA)) |>
  dplyr::select(pos_team, def_pos_team, period, down, distance,
                yards_to_goal, play_type, yards_gained,
                EPA, wp_before, wpa, success) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 8) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

## Step 6: Compute EPA per play and success rate

Three filters turn raw play-by-play into a fair team comparison:

1. **Keep only real offensive snaps** — runs and passes (`rush == 1 | pass == 1`),
   dropping kickoffs, punts, penalties and timeouts.
2. **Keep only FBS-vs-FBS games.** The season file also contains games
   involving FCS teams; the `home_team_division` and `away_team_division`
   columns let you filter them.
3. **Drop garbage time.** Plays in blowouts tell you little about how good a
   team is. There is no single standard definition and no `garbage_time` column
   in this data; here we keep plays where the offense's win probability before
   the snap (`wp_before`) is between 10% and 90%.

```{r filter-plays}
plays <- pbp |>
  dplyr::filter(
    home_team_division == "fbs", away_team_division == "fbs",
    rush == 1 | pass == 1,
    !is.na(EPA),
    wp_before >= 0.10, wp_before <= 0.90
  )
```

Now summarise by offense and by defense. **EPA is always from the offense's
point of view**, so a defense's EPA/play *allowed* is better when it is lower.

```{r team-summary}
offense <- plays |>
  dplyr::group_by(team = pos_team) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    off_plays   = dplyr::n(),
    off_epa     = mean(EPA),
    off_success = mean(success),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

defense <- plays |>
  dplyr::group_by(team = def_pos_team) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    def_plays   = dplyr::n(),
    def_epa     = mean(EPA),
    def_success = mean(success),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

teams <- offense |>
  dplyr::inner_join(defense, by = "team") |>
  dplyr::filter(off_plays >= 200, def_plays >= 200) |>
  dplyr::mutate(net_epa = off_epa - def_epa) |>
  dplyr::arrange(dplyr::desc(net_epa))

teams |>
  dplyr::select(team, off_epa, off_success, def_epa, def_success, net_epa) |>
  dplyr::slice_head(n = 10) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, col.names = c("Team", "Off EPA/play", "Off success",
                                         "Def EPA/play", "Def success", "Net EPA/play"))
```

```{r summary-facts, include=FALSE}
top_team   <- teams$team[1]
n_teams    <- nrow(teams)
league_epa <- mean(plays$EPA)
league_sr  <- mean(plays$success)
```

Across these `r n_teams` FBS teams, the average non-garbage-time snap was worth
`r sprintf("%+.3f", league_epa)` EPA, and `r sprintf("%.1f%%", 100 * league_sr)`
of snaps were successful. `r top_team` had the best net EPA per play in
`r season`. The `200`-play minimum is there because per-play averages over small
samples are noisy.

These are **raw** numbers. They are not adjusted for opponent strength, so a team
with a soft schedule looks better than it is. Opponent adjustment is what
ratings such as SP+ do; see
[Part IV](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-iv.html) of
the expected points series for how much that matters.

## Step 7: Your first plot

The classic team-efficiency chart puts offense on one axis and defense on the
other. We flip the defensive axis so that **up and to the right is good on both
sides of the ball**.

```{r epa-plot, fig.alt="Scatter plot of offensive EPA per play against defensive EPA per play allowed for FBS teams; teams in the upper right are good on both sides of the ball."}
label_teams <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::slice_head(teams, n = 8),
  dplyr::slice_tail(teams, n = 4)
)

ggplot(teams, aes(x = off_epa, y = def_epa)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = mean(teams$def_epa), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = mean(teams$off_epa), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(colour = "#2c7fb8", alpha = 0.7, size = 2) +
  geom_text(data = label_teams, aes(label = team),
            size = 3, vjust = -0.8, check_overlap = TRUE) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(
    title    = paste(season, "FBS team efficiency"),
    subtitle = "EPA per play on runs and passes, FBS vs FBS, win probability 10-90%",
    x        = "Offensive EPA/play (higher is better)",
    y        = "Defensive EPA/play allowed (higher on chart is better)",
    caption  = "Data: cfbfastR::load_cfb_pbp()"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
```

Want team logos instead of dots? The optional
[`cfbplotR`](https://cfbplotR.sportsdataverse.org/) package adds
`geom_cfb_logos()` (not run when this page is built, because the logos are
downloaded from external image hosts):

```{r logos, eval=FALSE}
if (requireNamespace("cfbplotR", quietly = TRUE)) {
  ggplot(teams, aes(x = off_epa, y = def_epa)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = mean(teams$def_epa), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    geom_vline(xintercept = mean(teams$off_epa), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
    cfbplotR::geom_cfb_logos(aes(team = team), width = 0.035) +
    scale_y_reverse() +
    labs(title = paste(season, "FBS team efficiency"),
         x = "Offensive EPA/play", y = "Defensive EPA/play allowed",
         caption = "Data: cfbfastR::load_cfb_pbp()") +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12)
}
```

## The core play-by-play columns

The season file has many columns; these are the ones you will use constantly.
Every name below is the exact column name in `load_cfb_pbp()` output.

**Identifiers**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `game_id` | unique ID for the game; join key to schedules |
| `drive_id` | unique ID for the drive within the game |
| `id_play` | unique ID for the play |
| `season`, `week` | season year and week number |
| `pos_team`, `def_pos_team` | the offense (team with the ball) and the defense |
| `home_team_division`, `away_team_division` | `"fbs"`, `"fcs"`, ... — use to restrict to FBS |

**Game situation**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `period` | quarter (5+ is overtime) |
| `down`, `distance` | down and yards needed for a first down |
| `yards_to_goal` | yards from the line of scrimmage to the opponent's end zone (75 = your own 25) |
| `play_type`, `play_text` | play category (`"Rush"`, `"Pass Reception"`, `"Sack"`, ...) and the raw description |
| `yards_gained` | yards gained on the play |
| `rush`, `pass` | 1 if the play was a run / a pass attempt or sack |

**Model outputs**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `ep_before`, `ep_after` | expected points before and after the play |
| `EPA` | expected points added: `ep_after - ep_before`, offense's view |
| `def_EPA` | the same number with the sign flipped, defense's view |
| `wp_before`, `wp_after` | the offense's win probability before and after the play |
| `wpa` | win probability added: `wp_after - wp_before` |
| `success` | 1 if the play gained 50% of the needed yards on 1st down, 70% on 2nd, 100% on 3rd or 4th; turnovers are never successful |
| `epa_success` | 1 if `EPA > 0` — an alternative definition of success |

**Handy flags**

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `rz_play` | 1 if the snap was inside the opponent's 20 (`yards_to_goal <= 20`) |
| `scoring_opp` | 1 if inside the opponent's 40 (`yards_to_goal <= 40`) |
| `stuffed_run` | 1 if a run gained zero or negative yards |
| `middle_8` | `TRUE` in the last four minutes of the first half and the first four of the second |

### Garbage time

There is **no `garbage_time` column** in `load_cfb_pbp()` output, so you choose
the rule. Two common options:

- **Win-probability window** (used above): keep `wp_before` between 0.10 and
  0.90. Simple and symmetric, and it adapts to the clock automatically.
- **Score and quarter**: drop plays where the score margin passes a threshold
  that tightens as the game goes on (a larger margin counts as garbage time in
  the second quarter than in the fourth). Versions of this rule, popularised by
  Bill Connelly, differ in their exact thresholds, so state the ones you use.

Several `cfbd_*()` functions, such as
[`cfbd_stats_season_advanced()`](../reference/cfbd_stats_season_advanced.html) and
[`cfbd_metrics_ppa_teams()`](../reference/cfbd_metrics_ppa_teams.html), take an
`excl_garbage_time` argument that applies CFBD's own definition server-side.

## Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|---|---|
| **EP** (expected points) | The net points the offense can expect from the current down, distance, field position, time and score before the next score of the half. Negative deep in your own territory, around +4 inside the opponent's 20. See [Part I](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-i.html). |
| **EPA** (expected points added) | The change in EP across one play. The single best per-play measure of offensive value. See [Part IV](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-iv.html). |
| **EPA/play** | Mean EPA over a set of plays: efficiency. **Total EPA** is the sum: volume. |
| **PPA** (predicted points added) | CollegeFootballData.com's name for its own EPA-style metric (the `cfbd_metrics_ppa_*()` functions). Built from a different model, so values will not match `cfbfastR` EPA exactly. |
| **WP** (win probability) | The probability the offense wins the game from the current state. See [Part V](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-v.html). |
| **WPA** (win probability added) | The change in WP across one play. Rewards plays that matter in close, late situations; EPA does not care about the scoreboard as much. |
| **Success rate** | Share of plays that are successful by the 50% / 70% / 100% rule above. Measures consistency. |
| **Explosiveness** | How big the successful plays are. CFBD defines it as average PPA on successful plays; others use the share of 20+ yard gains. |
| **Havoc rate** | Share of a defense's snaps with a tackle for loss, forced fumble, interception or pass breakup. Available from `cfbd_stats_season_advanced()` and `cfbd_game_box_advanced()`. |
| **Garbage time** | Plays where the outcome is effectively decided; usually excluded from efficiency stats. |
| **`yards_to_goal`** | Distance to the opponent's end zone. 75 means your own 25; 1 means the opponent's 1. |
| **Drive** | A sequence of plays by one team from when it gains possession until it scores, punts, turns the ball over or the half ends. |
| **Red zone** | Inside the opponent's 20 (`rz_play == 1`). |
| **Scoring opportunity** | A drive that reaches the opponent's 40 (`scoring_opp == 1`). |
| **Middle 8** | The last four minutes of the first half plus the first four of the second, when possessions can swing the game. |
| **CPOE** | Completion percentage over expected, from the completion probability model. See [Part VI](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-vi.html). |
| **SP+** | Bill Connelly's opponent-adjusted efficiency rating, via `cfbd_ratings_sp()`. |
| **SRS, Elo, FPI** | Other team ratings: simple rating system (margin adjusted for schedule), Elo (game-by-game rating updates) and ESPN's Football Power Index. See the [ratings functions](../reference/cfbd_ratings.html) and [`espn_ratings_fpi()`](../reference/espn_ratings_fpi.html). |

## All articles

**The Expected Points Model series** — read these in order once you are
comfortable with the example above.

| Article | What it covers |
|---|---|
| [Part I: How the Model Works](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-i.html) | what expected points means and the seven next-score outcomes the model predicts |
| [Part II: How the Model Is Built](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-ii.html) | why EP is a multiclass problem and how the model moved to eight gradient-boosted features |

| [Part VI: The Derived Models](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-vi.html) | CPOE, expected pass rate, field goals, two-point tries, fourth downs and QBR |

| Article | What it covers |

| [Visualizing Recruiting Geography](map-tutorial.html) | mapping where blue-chip recruits come from |
| [Team Talent from Recruiting Rankings](nth-rated-recruit.html) | approximating each school's recruited talent with `ggplot2` |
| [Simulating a Season with cfbseedR](cfbseedR-season-simulation.html) | rebuilding conference standings and the playoff field, then simulating the rest of a season |
| [PBP Pull Comparison](tutorials/pbp-pull-comparison.html) | play-by-play pulls compared across `cfbfastR` and the archived `cfbscrapR` |

## Where to go next

- **Go deeper on the metrics.** Read [Part IV (EPA)](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-iv.html)
  and [Part V (win probability)](college-football-expected-points-model-fundamentals-part-v.html).
- **Split the example.** Add `pass` or `rush` to the `group_by()` to get passing
  and rushing EPA separately, or group by `week` to see how a team changed over
  the season.
- **Go player-level.** `passer_player_name`, `rusher_player_name` and
  `receiver_player_name` let you compute EPA per dropback or per carry.
- **Join more data.** [`load_cfb_schedules()`](../reference/load_cfb_schedules.html),
  [`load_cfb_rosters()`](../reference/load_cfb_rosters.html) and
  [`load_cfb_teams()`](../reference/load_cfb_teams.html) join to play-by-play on
  `game_id` and team names.
- **Store every season locally.** [`update_cfb_db()`](../reference/update_cfb_db.html)
  builds a database of all play-by-play since 2014 so you only download new games.
- **Get help.** Browse the [reference index](../reference/index.html), file
  issues on [GitHub](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/cfbfastR/issues), and
  share your work tagged [@cfbfastR](https://x.com/cfbfastR).

## **Citation**

To cite the [**`cfbfastR`**](https://cfbfastR.sportsdataverse.org/) R package in publications, use `citation("cfbfastR")`, or:

BibTeX Citation

```bibtex
@misc{cfbfastr,
  author = {Saiem Gilani and Akshay Easwaran and Jared Lee and Eric Hess},
  title = {cfbfastR: Access College Football Play by Play Data},
  url = {https://cfbfastR.sportsdataverse.org/},
  doi = {10.32614/CRAN.package.cfbfastR},
  year = {2026}
}
```

## **Related SportsDataverse packages**

-   [**cfbfastR**](https://cfbfastR.sportsdataverse.org/) - college football
-   [**hoopR**](https://hoopR.sportsdataverse.org/) - men's basketball
-   [**wehoop**](https://wehoop.sportsdataverse.org/) - women's basketball
-   [**baseballr**](https://baseballr.sportsdataverse.org/) - baseball
-   [**fastRhockey**](https://fastRhockey.sportsdataverse.org/) - hockey
-   [**oddsapiR**](https://oddsapiR.sportsdataverse.org/) - betting odds
-   [**cfbseedR**](https://cfbseedR.sportsdataverse.org/) - college football season and playoff simulation (CRAN)
-   [**cfb4th**](https://cfb4th.sportsdataverse.org/) - college football fourth-down decisions (r-universe)
-   [**sdvplotR**](https://sdvplotR.sportsdataverse.org/) - team logos, colours and tables for every SportsDataverse league (r-universe)
-   [**sportyR**](https://sportyR.sportsdataverse.org/) - playing surfaces, including the college football field (CRAN)
-   [**cfbplotR**](https://cfbplotR.sportsdataverse.org/) - college football logos and colours (r-universe)
-   [**sportsdataverse-py**](https://py.sportsdataverse.org/) - the Python package
-   [**sportsdataverse-R**](https://r.sportsdataverse.org/) - the R meta-package
